title: India Face Must-Win Hockey World Cup Match Against Pakistan After England Loss
excerpt: India's 2-4 defeat to England in Pool D leaves Harmanpreet Singh's side needing at least a draw against Pakistan on Wednesday to stay in the tournament.
body:
• India lost 2-4 to England in their second Pool D match at the 2026 Hockey World Cup, despite leading 2-1 at halftime
  • A win or draw against Pakistan on Wednesday will keep India's second-round hopes alive
  • A loss to Pakistan would eliminate India from the tournament regardless of other results
  • England lead Pool D with six points from two wins, while India sit second with three points

India's campaign at the 2026 Hockey World Cup hit a significant setback on Monday when England fought back from a halftime deficit to win 4-2 in their Pool D encounter, according to Times of India. India now face an elimination scenario heading into their final group match against Pakistan on Wednesday.

How England Turned the Match Around

India appeared in control after captain Harmanpreet Singh and Dilpreet Singh scored to give the side a 2-1 lead at the break, having absorbed an early goal from England's Bandurak. But the second half belonged to England, who dominated the third quarter with goals from Rushmere and Croft before Bandurak added his second in the final period to seal a comprehensive 4-2 victory.

India's defensive lapses proved costly, with the team unable to contain England's attacking momentum after the interval. England converted their chances with clinical precision while India struggled to create openings in the second half.

Qualification Scenarios for India

The mathematics are straightforward for India, who now sit on three points from two matches. The top two teams from each pool advance to the second round, while the bottom two are consigned to classification matches for 9th through 16th place.

A win against Pakistan would take India to six points and guarantee qualification regardless of the England-Wales result. A draw would lift India to four points, which would likely be enough — India would advance as long as Wales do not beat England, or if they do, India's goal difference holds up. A loss, however, would be terminal. Pakistan would leapfrog India in the standings, and India would be unable to finish in the top two.

"India had started their campaign with a 3-1 win over Wales but defensive mistakes against England proved costly in the second half."

— Times of India

Pool D Standings

England sit atop Pool D with a perfect six points from two matches. India are second with three points after their opening win over Wales. Pakistan and Wales are level on one point each from two games, meaning Pakistan also have everything to play for in Wednesday's clash.

The Diaspora Angle

An India-Pakistan hockey match carries enormous significance for the South Asian diaspora worldwide, evoking decades of rivalry that extends far beyond the pitch. For Indian hockey fans in the United States, United Kingdom, and Canada, the high-stakes nature of this fixture — with elimination on the line — adds an extra layer of intensity to what is always one of the most-watched matchups in the sport.

What's Next

India will take on Pakistan in their final Pool D match on Wednesday. Captain Harmanpreet Singh, who has been one of India's standout performers, will need his side to address the defensive vulnerabilities exposed by England. The match is effectively a knockout fixture for both teams, with the loser facing elimination from the main tournament bracket.
